chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Tupelo and Vicksburg: the singer Linda and the white promoter
summary: Collins and the light-skinned vocalist were harassed by white men in Tupelo, and in Vicksburg the promoter terrorized her in her room.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: That was a girl vocalist with the group. Her name was Linda something, I don't know, and she liked me, you know. So we played a town called Tupelo, Mississippi, and this girl had to -- she was a very attractive girl, she was a mulatto girl, you know, very light. And she had to send a telegram or something and she wanted me to walk down town with her, so

we -- I've walked, and on our way back there were a car full of white guys and they would drive along and just as we were going to cross the intersection they would stop and park in front of us and we would have to walk around the car. And they were making all kind of remarks, you know.

So this continued every block until we got back where we lived, and when we got to this rooming house the lady who ran the rooming house, she was sitting on the porch and they pulled up in front of there and called her out and told her that they wanted this girl. So she said, well I'll tell you what you do. You come back after the concert tonight and we'll see that, you know --

Well, what had to happen. We left right after the concert, we had to leave town. This is why. We played another town, Vicksburg, Mississippi, and Linda left -- we usually played say the last three numbers without the vocalist, you know, so this night I think she said she had a headache or something and she was going to go home. Well, we lived about two blocks from the auditorium where we were appearing, and after the -- after we finished I went -- we all lived in the same place. I went in, I left the thing, the concert and went home, and as I started to go upstairs in the rooming house this white guy burst out of Linda's room and ran by me, and I recognized the promoter. And he had terrorized this girl, and the land lady. This is what I mean, I was so glad
out of there because you had no -- you know, if you fight back you're dead.
